You're describing **pure SaaS** — software that's already modular by design (seats, tiers, feature flags, usage limits). The "intelligent clay" metaphor is for service businesses where the offering is delivered by humans and is currently too custom/bespoke to scale. Your product is the opposite problem: it's already a product.

**What you're likely actually asking about** (and where to go instead):

- **Packaging & tier design for SaaS** → frameworks like Kyle Poyar's "Good/Better/Best" or Patrick Campbell's value-metric work (ProfitWell/Paddle). The core move is picking the right *value metric* (seats vs. projects vs. automations vs. storage) and gating features against jobs-to-be-done, not decomposing atoms.
- **Feature-to-tier assignment** → differentiation analysis: which features are *access* (gate behind tier), which are *usage* (meter and charge), which are *table stakes* (give to everyone).
- **Enterprise unbundling** → if "custom Enterprise" is a black box hiding 4-5 repeatable add-ons (SSO, audit logs, SLA, dedicated CSM, advanced permissions), those become named add-ons or a defined Business tier between Pro and Enterprise. That's the closest analog to what this skill does — but the methodology is SaaS packaging, not service productization.
- **Freemium-to-paid conversion mechanics** → separate discipline; look at activation events and natural expansion triggers.

**Where this skill *would* apply to your business:** if you also sell **implementation services, onboarding packages, customer success retainers, or done-for-you setup** alongside the software — those are services and can be productized. If that's part of the picture, tell me about the services side and I'll run the blueprint on that.

Otherwise, you want a SaaS pricing/packaging resource, not this one.

You're describing a **pure physical product**, not a service. There's no time, no expertise delivery, no configurable process to decompose into atoms. A finished wallet on a shelf is already the atom.

## What you probably actually want

One of these three, depending on your goal:

1. **SKU + bundle logic** — variants (leather type, thread color, monogram, card slots, coin pocket) priced as add-ons on a base wallet. This is product configuration, not service productization. Shopify/WooCommerce handle this natively.

2. **Tiered product line** — Good/Better/Best across your catalog (e.g., Bifold $95 / Cardholder+Bifold $120 / Handstitched Heritage $220). Different problem, different skill.

3. **Service layer *around* the product** — if you offer **custom commissions**, **repair/restoration**, **corporate gifting programs**, or **leather care subscriptions**, *those* are services and I can modularize them. A commission service ("send me a photo of your dad's old belt, I'll make a wallet from matched leather") is exactly the kind of thing this skill decomposes well.

## Redirect

- For #1 (SKU/variant structure): any e-commerce configurator guide — not this skill.
- For #2 (product-line tiering): a pricing/merchandising skill.
- For #3 (services around the product): **come back here** and describe the service. For example: *"I take custom wallet commissions — clients send me references, we go back and forth on design, I source leather, hand-stitch it, and ship in 4–8 weeks. Currently charging $300 flat and it's eating my time."* That I can decompose into atoms, dimensions, and tiers.

Want to try #3? Tell me about any service you offer alongside the wallets.

# Part 2 — Configuration Architecture

| Dimension | What it controls | Levels | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| **License Scope** | Who can use it and for what | Personal / Team (≤10 seats) / Agency (unlimited internal) / Reseller (client-facing) | Reseller requires White-Label = On; Reseller blocks Community-only support |
| **Vertical Depth** | Domain-specific dimension packs + benchmark data | Generic only / +1 pack / All packs (rolling) | All packs requires Rolling updates |
| **Support Level** | Human review of user's blueprint runs | Community / Async review / Live review / Embedded expert | Live review requires Team+; Embedded requires Agency+ |
| **Configurator Export** | Machine-readable output for external builders | None / JSON only / One platform template / All templates + custom schema help | Custom schema help requires Async review or higher |
| **Update Cadence** | Version stream subscribed to | Frozen (pinned version) / Rolling minor / Rolling + preview of next major | Reseller requires Rolling minimum |
| **Branding** | Whose name is on the skill output | Intelligent Clay attributed / Co-branded / White-labeled | White-labeled requires Agency+ |
| **Memory Integration** | Persistent-memory adapters | None / claude-mem / Custom backend (BYO) | Custom backend requires Team+ |
| **Human Time** | Live sessions with maintainer | None / Audit call / Co-working session / Cohort seat / 1-on-1 engagement | Cohort and 1-on-1 are mutually exclusive |

**Invalid combinations the configurator must block:**
- Reseller license + Community-only support (can't resell an unsupported product)
- White-label + Frozen updates (white-labelers need the latest anti-patterns)
- Personal license + White-label (no downstream clients to brand for)
- All-vertical packs + Frozen updates (packs ship in minor versions)
- Embedded expert + Personal license (economics don't work)
- 1-on-1 engagement + Cohort seat (double-billed human time)

# Part 3 — Three Tiers + Build-Your-Own

Renamed in-vocabulary: **Free Core**, **Practitioner**, **Studio**, **Foundry**. (The MIT skill remains free; paid tiers wrap it.)

### Free Core — the MIT skill *(unchanged, permanent)*
- **Configuration:** Personal license · Generic dimensions only · Community support · No configurator export · Frozen or rolling (user's choice via git) · Attributed branding · Optional claude-mem · No human time
- **Positioning:** For the individual consultant or curious builder who wants to productize their own offering, once, in public.
- **Pricing logic:** $0. Anchored against every other open-source Claude skill. The free tier is the top of the funnel and the credibility engine — never gate the core blueprint generator.

### Practitioner — $B/year *(entry paid tier)*
- **Configuration:** Team license (≤10 seats) · +1 vertical pack of choice · Async blueprint review (48h, 5/mo) · JSON configurator export · Rolling minor updates · Attributed · claude-mem included · 1 audit call/quarter
- **Positioning:** For the solo consultant or small team who runs the skill on real client offerings and wants a human sanity-check on the output before shipping.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against a single day of the user's own consulting rate — if one blueprint review saves one bad tier decision, it pays for itself. Placeholder `+$B` until niche is named; likely lands in the $B ≈ single-seat pro-tool range ($500–2,000/yr equivalent).

### Studio — $C/year *(flagship)*
- **Configuration:** Agency license (unlimited internal) · All vertical packs (rolling) · Live blueprint review (2/mo) · One platform configurator template (Typeform *or* Webflow *or* Airtable) · Rolling + preview · Co-branded · claude-mem + custom-backend eligible · Quarterly co-working session + cohort seat
- **Positioning:** For the agency or productization consultancy that uses Intelligent Clay across many client engagements and needs it to feel like part of their stack.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against **one avoided misfired tier structure on one client engagement** — the failure cost the skill prevents. If Studio prevents one $50K engagement from being mispriced by 30%, ROI is obvious. Priced *below* the sum of BYO parts to reach this config (see flagship-protection below). Likely `+$C` ≈ mid-four-figures/yr.

### Foundry — $D/year + engagement fees *(reseller / white-label)*
- **Configuration:** Reseller license · All packs · Embedded expert (monthly) · All configurator templates + custom schema help · Rolling + preview · White-labeled · Custom memory backend · 1-on-1 productization engagement (quarterly)
- **Positioning:** For the agency, platform, or educator who wants to resell productization-as-a-service to their own clients under their own brand.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against **what the reseller charges their downstream clients** — Foundry is a revenue-share-adjacent license, priced as a floor + variable engagement fees. `+$D` is the license floor; real revenue is in the engagements.

### Build-Your-Own Framework

- **Base price:** Practitioner ($B/yr) — the floor for any paid access
- **Per-dimension upgrade pricing (placeholder tokens until niche-anchored):**
  - License Scope: Team → Agency = +$X₁ · Agency → Reseller = +$X₂
  - Vertical Depth: +1 pack = +$X₃/pack · All packs = +$X₄
  - Support: Async → Live = +$X₅ · Live → Embedded = +$X₆
  - Configurator: JSON → One template = +$X₇ · All templates = +$X₈
  - Updates: Rolling → Preview = +$X₉
  - Branding: Attributed → Co-branded = +$X₁₀ · Co-branded → White-label = +$X₁₁

- **Floor:** $B/yr (Practitioner base). Below this, route to Free Core.

- **Flagship-protection rule:** BYO-summing to reach Studio's exact config must exceed Studio's flagship price by ≥20%. Same for Foundry vs. its BYO-equivalent. Practitioner is the floor and doesn't need protection — it's the anchor everything else is priced against.
